historical_context.time_period: Kalsa's standing present; the exact date and calendar remain unresolved.
historical_context.location: The Cistern House at Low Sere, centered on the stone lip between the live east basin and drained west inspection basin above the Ashen Intake pressure door.
historical_context.summary: A lower-step water witness opens Low Sere's first three-copy technical challenge during an ordinary intake watch. A failing shutter turns record custody, neutral comparison, emergency authority, and provisional succession into immediate choices.

public_facts.text: Low Sere is a forty-one-hearth settlement whose warmth, drinking water, crops, craft, and trade depend on an old intake beneath the Cistern House.
The basin table joins water witnesses, Grey Bed workers, maintainers, and the intake custodian without becoming a universal village government.
Sera holds the technical spindle, Maro controls the settlement's drain access, Ressa can make a bounded comparison, and Teren's removal and appeal remain disputed.
Techpriest lineages carry practical memory and real leverage, but technical competence does not automatically grant land, water, or political rule.

ambient_pressures.text: A technical challenge consumes specialist travel, food, work time, and remaining safe interval; redress must therefore preserve petitioners materially as well as on paper.
An independent comparer can have future institutional interests. Declared conflict narrows authority; it does not make interests disappear.
Emergency political action may continue only as a named override within split keys and material stops; it cannot convert a machine response into a verdict.
Teren's appeal, Sera's permanent appointment, and any future Eighth Baffle role remain unresolved across all branch outcomes.

groups.label: Lower-step households and Grey Bed workers
institutional_logic: Make water, heat, crop flow, work loss, and unsafe notice visible before upper-hearth priority turns them into private hardship.
material_incentives: Keep minimum water and warmth, preserve crop labor, receive wages or replacement for hearing time, and keep an outside copy of any claim.
internal_virtues: Evidence that remains attached to the harmed place
internal_shames: Allowing Grey Bed work to become nonessential only when rationing begins
prestige_markers: A work chain that survives elite retelling
Water carried for households with no private vessels
taboo_triggers: Being treated as raw data for a specialist's conclusion
emotional_display_norms: Anger arrives as concrete comparison, dry jokes, named labor, and refusal to let the bowl leave the table.
trust_defaults: Trusts duplicated records, visible samples, other workers, and specialists who declare their limits.

groups.label: Low Sere basin table
institutional_logic: Coordinate water, shared stores, maintenance labor, threshold admission, and emergency basin action without absorbing unrelated household or technical authority.
material_incentives: Keep the settlement habitable, preserve a functioning operator, ration scarce flow, and prevent review from consuming the final safe interval.
internal_virtues: Decisions that name who must carry them
internal_shames: A public work stopped by indecision
A stranger acquiring the intake through procedure
prestige_markers: Stores that cover a failed intervention
A decision that survives the next work-watch
taboo_triggers: A custodian using safety as hereditary monopoly
A petitioner consuming time without visible evidence
emotional_display_norms: Fear becomes scheduling, ration marks, and urgency; guilt prefers to call itself continuity.
trust_defaults: Trusts the people already keeping service alive, then worries that this is exactly how permanent provisional power happens.

groups.label: Low Sere's intake custodians
institutional_logic: Preserve bounded operational competence, material stops, service records, and a safe handoff for one named configuration.
material_incentives: Keep access to the spindle, receive household support, recover missing tools and records, and avoid being made liable for political overrides.
internal_shames: Letting a public system fail through private custody
A provisional office mistaken for incompetence
prestige_markers: A successor who can explain the changed machine
taboo_triggers: A council taking the spindle as if access created competence
A rival lineage treating comparison as succession
emotional_display_norms: Fear is narrowed into system boundaries; resentment appears as exact statements of what the office does not own.
trust_defaults: Trusts material state and witnessed practice; distrusts universal titles and retrospective certainty.

groups.label: Eighth Baffle comparison practice
institutional_logic: Trade portable competence and cross-site records for passage, support, recognition, and future work while keeping findings inside proven scope.
material_incentives: Receive travel costs, lodging, fees, copied records, and possibly a later support compact without acquiring title through one hearing.
internal_virtues: Surviving the patron who dislikes the finding
internal_shames: Using neutral witness status to inherit an appointment
Certifying a system from prestigious words alone
prestige_markers: A diagnosis another lineage can reproduce
A public limit kept under pressure
A handoff that preserves adverse evidence
taboo_triggers: Being ordered to call a political act safe
Having specialist work treated as free devotion
emotional_display_norms: Self-interest is safer when named; professional anger appears as refusal to let machine response settle human jurisdiction.
trust_defaults: Trusts three-handed records and specific competencies; expects hosts to want a verdict faster than the evidence permits.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Every delayed appointment risks the water, while every emergency handoff risks becoming permanent through use.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Make succession choices transfer specific keys, support, copies, and duties; never let the word temporary do the work alone.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A hearing that costs a work-watch, water, food, or shelter can exclude the people most exposed to failure while remaining formally open.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Tie copies, witnesses, ration standing, hearing time, and evacuation membership to later options and endings.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: An itinerant comparer needs fees, lodging, route access, and future work; independence is produced by disclosed limits and separated custody, not purity.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Let Ressa state her material interests plainly and make the player decide how those interests narrow her seat.

role_pressure_fields.summary: Bel Orra carries material observations and household loss into a forum that can record them but may prefer a faster specialist answer.
obligations: Keep lower-step water and standing visible
Choose who holds the outside copy
failure_modes: Borrowing Maro's authority until he owns the petition
Winning a record after her household can no longer use it
Being treated as evidence rather than a claimant

role_pressure_fields.summary: Sera Venn preserves reduced service with incomplete formation records and a deliberately bounded grant.
obligations: Refuse the Intake Crown beyond evidence
Surrender copies and specific access under review
Seek an honest appointment or replacement
failure_modes: Clinging to access because no successor is safe
Letting the table translate degraded service into full competence
Treating local workers as nontechnical scenery

role_pressure_fields.summary: Ressa Orr can compare part of the intake practice, but her fee and lineage's possible future compact create visible interests.
failure_modes: Letting urgency shrink the stated boundary
Confusing transborder reputation with local jurisdiction

role_pressure_fields.summary: Maro Seln owns basin access, schedules, and emergency settlement action while lacking technical authority over the pressure seal.
failure_modes: Using speed to own the petition
Making lower-step loss disappear inside settlement survival

role_pressure_fields.summary: Teren Vey has relevant technical memory, no threshold control, a disputed removal, and a self-created evidence hostage below.
obligations: Answer for the Grey Scald intervention
Surrender or enable review of withheld records
failure_modes: Making every valid criticism serve reinstatement
Using the missing folio to starve review

known_context.text: Bel knows lower-step water, wet walls, work loss, basin routine, and the visible authority of the people at the lip.

beliefs.text: Bel believes a claim must remain in more than one hand if it is to survive urgency.

misreads.text: Bel may treat an itinerant lineage's future interest as present capture before the appointment actually moves.

must_not_know.text: Bel does not know the Ashen Intake's hidden formula solution, the cause of its knocks, or the result of any future descent.

known_context.text: Sera knows degraded service above the pressure door, the limits of her grant, Teren's surviving practice, and which missing objects prevent Crown comparison.

beliefs.text: Sera believes a provisional office should end in a bounded appointment or an honest replacement, not indefinite liability.

misreads.text: Sera may hear a commoner's demand for outside copies as the basin table preparing her replacement.

must_not_know.text: Sera cannot certify the Intake Crown without recovering and comparing the Ashen Measure and handoff folio.

known_context.text: Ressa knows part of the intake's filter and pressure practice and can compare Sera's formation and Teren's act only inside that scope.

beliefs.text: Ressa believes declared interest and reproducible comparison are stronger than claims of disinterested purity.

misreads.text: Ressa may underestimate how quickly paid comparison can become foreign succession in a frightened settlement.

must_not_know.text: Ressa cannot treat an accepted formula, lineage reputation, or isolated success as proof of legal authority or full intake competence.

author_only_boundaries.text: The three-copy challenge is an authored local elaboration for Low Sere, not a universal Techpriest court, rank, or transborder law.
All endings are branch-local fixture outcomes. None settles Teren's appeal, Sera's permanent appointment, Eighth Baffle succession, or the Ashen Intake's canonical future.
The fixture may show knocks, grit, pressure, and human interpretation but must not decide whether the dead, a divine presence, or machinery caused any answer.
